name: Shubayqa bread-like food
description: Natufian inhabitants of Shubayqa 1 produced bread-like foodstuffs, evidenced by charred remains recovered from fireplaces.

impact.note: Charred remains at one site showing a new kind of food made from wild cereals; no descent to later bread is shown.

date.label: About 14,400–14,200 cal BP (12,450–12,250 BCE)
date.basis: Seven short-lived plant samples from the fireplaces provide the authors’ approximate 14,400–14,200 cal BP contextual estimate; associated occupation estimates are wider at two sigma.

events.statement: Natufian inhabitants of Shubayqa 1 produced bread-like foodstuffs, evidenced by charred remains recovered from fireplaces.
events.caveats: The remains are interpreted as bread-like; exact ingredients and preparation varied. The dates are for hearth contexts, not the global invention of bread. A published model gives a wider two-sigma range for initial site occupation; this approximate fireplace estimate is not a hard bound.

evidence.supports: Bread-like remains were found in hearths dated by short-lived plant remains to approximately 14,400–14,200 cal BP.
Charred bread-like remains in Early Natufian fireplaces are interpreted as products made by the site’s inhabitants.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest evidence currently researched for this scoped record; not a claim of global priority. The remains are interpreted as bread-like; exact ingredients and preparation varied. The dates are for hearth contexts, not the global invention of bread.
